issues.legal_issue: State rulemaking authority over minor minerals does not extend to prohibiting the interstate movement of minerals that have already been lawfully excavated.
material_facts: The challenged rules prohibited sand from being transported beyond the State’s borders, including sand excavated under valid leases and accompanied by authorized transport documents.
The rules applied after excavation and restricted the movement or sale of the excavated sand outside the State.
The appeals challenged the High Court’s decision striking down the rules.
issues.conclusion: The rules exceeded the State’s delegated rulemaking powers and were ultra vires the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 15(1) and 15(1A) of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957 authorize rules concerning the grant and regulation of mineral concessions, but do not authorize control over minor minerals after excavation, including their sale or movement outside the State. Section 23-C authorizes rules to prevent illegal mining, transportation and storage; read in light of its object, it does not authorize restrictions on transporting legally excavated minerals. M.P.P. Kavery Chetty v. State of Tamil Nadu, (1995) 2 SCC 402, and K.T. Varghese v. State of Kerala, (2008) 3 SCC 735, establish the limits on control over minerals after excavation. D.K. Trivedi & Sons v. State of Gujarat, 1986 Supp SCC 20, and State of Tamil Nadu v. Hind Stone, (1981) 2 SCC 205, concern measures connected to the grant or refusal of leases; Hind Stone permits prohibition as regulation where it has a direct nexus with mineral conservation and exploitation, unlike a ban on movement after lawful excavation.

predicates.appeal_challenges_mineral_transport_rule: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a rule governing the transport of minerals.
predicates.mineral_was_lawfully_excavated: A leaseholder excavated the mineral under valid authorization.
predicates.rule_bars_post_excavation_interstate_mov: The rule prohibits the mineral from being transported across a state border after excavation.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a mineral-transport rule and the rule bars interstate movement of lawfully excavated minerals after excavation, the rule exceeds the delegated power to make rules about minerals.

issues.legal_issue: A state-imposed prohibition on interstate movement of goods violates the constitutional freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse when imposed without a constitutionally authorized basis for restricting that freedom.
material_facts: The rules barred sand from moving beyond the State’s borders, restricting the interstate movement of goods.
The State imposed the prohibition through rules made under mineral legislation rather than through a state law enacted with the required constitutional safeguards.
The material relied on by the State focused on restricting exports outside India, and no scarcity justification for restricting movement between States was established.
issues.conclusion: The rules violated Part XIII of the Constitution, including Article 301, and were invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Article 301 protects freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India. Articles 302 to 304 set out the constitutional framework for restrictions and differentiation: Parliament may impose restrictions in the public interest under Article 302, Article 303 limits preferences and discrimination between States subject to the stated scarcity provision, and a State’s restrictions under Article 304(b) require the prescribed legislative process and prior presidential sanction. Part XIII is a code of checks and balances intended to facilitate a common market and economic integration while permitting justified restrictions. Video Electronics Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Punjab, (1990) 3 SCC 87, explains that economic unity and balanced development must be considered together within that framework.

predicates.appeal_challenges_interstate_trade_restr: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a restriction on trade between States.
predicates.state_rule_bans_interstate_movement_of_g: The State imposed a rule prohibiting goods from moving across its border.
predicates.restriction_was_imposed_without_authoriz: The State imposed the restriction by executive rule rather than through legislation satisfying the applicable constitutional requirements.
predicates.scarcity_justification_was_not_establish: The State did not establish that scarcity justified restricting interstate movement of the goods.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a state rule that bans interstate movement of goods, the restriction lacks the required legislative basis, and scarcity is not established, the rule violates the constitutional freedom of interstate trade.
